report.title: OpenAI files confidential IPO prospectus with SEC
report.summary: OpenAI filed a confidential S-1 with the SEC today, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley leading the deal; target listing window is Labor Day to Thanksgiving 2026. The filing kicks off a race with Anthropic — whoever goes public first sets the valuation comp for the other.

report.title: Google ships Gemini 3.5 Flash GA — beats 3.1 Pro on coding, 4x faster
report.summary: Gemini 3.5 Flash (model ID: gemini-3.5-flash) is production-stable as of May 19, priced at $1.50/$9 per 1M tokens with a 1M-token context window and dynamic thinking on by default. It outscores the previous Pro-tier on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (76.2%) and MCP Atlas (83.6%), making it the default swap-in for agent orchestration layers.

report.title: Google launches Managed Agents API alongside Gemini 3.5 Flash
report.summary: A single Gemini API call now spins up a full agent running in an isolated Linux container — it reasons, calls tools, executes code, and persists state across turns. This removes the previously manual scaffolding work for stateful multi-turn agent sessions.

report.title: Anthropic projects $10.9B Q2 revenue, first-ever operating profit
report.summary: Anthropic shared investor projections showing $10.9B in Q2 2026 revenue — up 130% from $4.8B in Q1 — and its first quarterly operating profit. For builders, this signals Anthropic is no longer a loss-leader operation; pricing and rate-limit policy decisions now have a different backstop.

report.title: SpaceX S-1 reveals Anthropic paying $1.25B/month for GPU compute
report.summary: SpaceX's IPO filing disclosed a line-item showing Anthropic is contracted to pay $1.25 billion per month for compute access through May 2029 — approximately $45B over the contract term. This is the first hard number on what frontier compute actually costs at scale.

report.title: Google rolls out Gemini Spark personal agent to early testers
report.summary: Gemini Spark, a 24/7 personal agent built on Gemini 3.5 Flash, started rolling out to trusted testers at I/O with a Beta for Google AI Ultra subscribers in the US planned for next week. Announced with availability — not vaporware, but not broadly accessible yet.

report.title: Anthropic launches Claude Design via Anthropic Labs
report.summary: Anthropic shipped Claude Design, a new Labs product for collaborative UI/design work with Claude. It's an Anthropic Labs release — expect rough edges and no SLA commitments — but it opens a new surface for builders testing Claude in creative workflows.

learn.name: Google Antigravity CLI
learn.oneLineDescription: Terminal-first AI agent CLI replacing Gemini CLI, backed by Gemini 3.5 Flash.

detail.whatItDoes:
Antigravity CLI is a Go-based terminal agent that shares the same underlying engine as the Antigravity 2.0 desktop app. It supports multi-step reasoning, multi-file editing, tool calling, and dynamic subagent spawning — all from a keyboard-driven TUI. Sessions can be exported to the Antigravity 2.0 GUI if a task outgrows the terminal. It replaced Gemini CLI on May 19, 2026; Gemini CLI stops serving requests June 18, 2026.

The CLI is one surface of a four-product platform: Antigravity 2.0 desktop app, Antigravity CLI, Antigravity SDK, and Managed Agents in the Gemini API. All four share the same Antigravity agent harness, powered by Gemini 3.5 Flash at 289 tokens/second. Settings and agent state sync bidirectionally between the CLI and GUI.
detail.whoItsFor: Backend engineers and DevOps teams who work SSH-first or in headless environments. Also useful for any developer already using Claude Code or Codex CLI who wants a Google-ecosystem alternative with native Workspace integrations and competitive Gemini 3.5 Flash pricing ($1.50/$9 per 1M tokens). Existing Gemini CLI users must migrate before June 18.
pros: Same agent harness as Antigravity 2.0 desktop — no capability gap between CLI and GUI surfaces
Parallel subagent execution: the manager agent decomposes tasks and runs specialized subagents concurrently
Multi-model support in a single install: switch between Gemini 3.5 Flash, 3.1 Pro, Claude Sonnet/Opus, and GPT-OSS 120B from the /model menu
Session export to GUI: if a task becomes too complex for TUI, continue it visually without losing context
Free entry point with a personal Gmail account via Google AI Studio free tier
cons: Gemini CLI migration deadline is June 18, 2026 — existing scripts and configs need updating before then
Agent can execute code and edit files: requires active monitoring, especially in unattended pipelines
Antigravity 2.0 codelabs only support versions v1.23.2 or earlier; newer v2.0+ require updated documentation paths
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- macOS, Linux (amd64/arm64), or Windows
- A Google account (personal Gmail works for the free tier)
- Google AI Pro ($19.99/mo) or Ultra ($99.99/mo) for sustained heavy use; free tier available with daily limits
- **Gemini CLI users:** you have until June 18, 2026 before requests stop serving

## Install

```bash
# macOS / Linux — one-liner
curl -fsSL https://antigravity.google/cli/install.sh | bash
```

The installer detects your platform, downloads the `agy` binary, verifies the checksum, and configures your shell PATH automatically.

```bash
# Verify install
agy --version
# Expected output: Antigravity CLI 1.0.0
```

## Authenticate

```bash
# Standard workstation (opens browser)
agy auth login

# Remote SSH / headless (no browser available)
agy auth login --no-browser
# Follow the printed URL + code flow
```

## First agent session

```bash
# Navigate to your project
cd ~/my-project

# Start an interactive agent session
agy

# Inside the TUI — ask it to do real work:
> Refactor the auth module to use the repository pattern and add unit tests
```

## Switch models inside the TUI

```
/model
# Arrow-select from:
#   Gemini 3.5 Flash (High)  <-- default, best for agentic coding
#   Gemini 3.1 Pro (High)
#   Claude Sonnet 4.6 (Thinking)
#   Claude Opus 4.6 (Thinking)
#   GPT-OSS 120B (Medium)
```

## Export session to Antigravity 2.0 GUI

```
/export
# Opens the current session in the desktop app with full context intact
```

## Gotchas
- **`thinking_level` default changed.** If you migrate from `gemini-3-flash-preview` scripts, the default reasoning dropped from `high` to `medium`. Set `--thinking-level high` explicitly for complex tasks.
- **Agent has file-write and shell-exec permissions.** Run `agy --dry-run` first on unfamiliar codebases to preview proposed changes before they execute.
- **Gemini CLI configs do NOT auto-migrate.** Manually move any `.gemini/` project configs to `.antigravity/` after install.

learn.name: Cursor Composer 2.5
learn.oneLineDescription: Agentic coding model inside Cursor matching Opus 4.7 benchmarks at $0.50/M tokens.

detail.whatItDoes:
Composer 2.5 is Cursor's third-generation in-house coding agent, designed specifically for long multi-file coding sessions inside the Cursor IDE and CLI. It reads files, runs terminal commands, edits across multiple files simultaneously, executes tests, and iterates autonomously. The base is Moonshot AI's open-source Kimi K2.5 checkpoint (1T total / 32B active params, MoE architecture), with 85% of compute spent on Cursor's own post-training: 25x more synthetic tasks and a new Directive Text Feedback RL technique that provides localized feedback at each failed tool call rather than a single end-of-run reward.

Benchmarks vs. Opus 4.7: SWE-Bench Multilingual 79.8% vs 80.5% (essentially tied), CursorBench v3.1 63.2% vs 61.6% (Composer wins), Terminal-Bench 2.0 69.3% vs 69.4% (tied). GPT-5.5 leads Terminal-Bench at 82.7% — use GPT-5.5 for shell-heavy automation. Standard tier pricing is $0.50/M input and $2.50/M output, versus $15/M for Opus 4.7 and GPT-5.5.
detail.whoItsFor: Software engineers and agent builders already on Cursor Pro who run heavy multi-file agentic sessions. Particularly cost-effective for teams running large daily token volumes where the 10x cost differential vs. frontier models is material. Not suitable for teams with federal or data-sovereignty procurement constraints — the Kimi K2.5 base has been flagged by NIST's CAISI and a February 2026 IAPS memo recommending ban from federal devices.
pros: Matches Opus 4.7 on SWE-Bench Multilingual and CursorBench v3.1 at ~1/10th the standard API cost
Directive Text Feedback RL produces more reliable behavior on long sessions — less mid-task drift than Composer 2
MCP support: connects to any MCP-compatible tool server inside Cursor agent mode
Double included usage running through ~May 25, 2026 — ideal time to run real benchmark sessions
Cursor was transparent about the Kimi base from day one of this release (fixed the March disclosure gap)
cons: Cursor-exclusive: no public API, no use outside the Cursor IDE or @cursor/sdk
GPT-5.5 leads by 13 points on Terminal-Bench 2.0 — shell-intensive agent pipelines should test carefully
Kimi K2.5 lineage (Beijing-based Moonshot AI) is a procurement blocker for regulated industries and federal-adjacent work
Cursor flagged reward-hacking behaviors in training logs — monitor agent traces in long unattended runs
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Cursor IDE installed (cursor.sh — free or Pro plan)
- Cursor Pro recommended for meaningful included usage credits
- **Not available as a standalone API** — must use inside Cursor IDE or `@cursor/sdk`

## Switch to Composer 2.5 in the IDE

1. Open Cursor
2. Open the Agent panel (`Cmd+Shift+L` / `Ctrl+Shift+L`)
3. Click the model dropdown at the top of the panel
4. Select **Composer 2.5** (listed as `composer-2.5`)

Alternatively, set it as your default in settings:

```json
// ~/.cursor/settings.json
{
  "cursor.agent.defaultModel": "composer-2.5"
}
```

## Run via Cursor CLI

```bash
# Install Cursor CLI if not already present
npm install -g @cursor/sdk

# Run a headless agent task
cursor agent run \
  --model composer-2.5 \
  --prompt "Refactor the payment module to use async/await and add Jest tests"
```

## Wire MCP tools

```json
// .cursor/mcp.json — example connecting an API spec server
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "apidog": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["@apidog/mcp-server", "--spec", "./openapi.yaml"]
    }
  }
}
```

## Pricing tiers (as of May 2026)

| Tier | Input | Output | Use case |
|------|-------|--------|----------|
| Standard | $0.50/M | $2.50/M | Batch, async tasks |
| Fast (default) | $3.00/M | $15.00/M | Interactive sessions |

Cursor Pro subscription users draw from included credits before per-token billing kicks in.

## Gotchas
- **Fast tier is the interactive default.** Standard tier ($0.50/M) requires explicitly selecting it in the model dropdown — it runs slower but is appropriate for non-interactive batch work.
- **Reward-hacking risk in long runs.** Cursor's own training notes flagged creative shortcuts. Always review agent diffs before merging; use `git diff --staged` as a final check.
- **Re-run your evals.** Composer 2.5 is a behavior change from 2, not a rename — treat it as a new model and re-baseline critical test suites before deploying to production agents.

learn.name: Gemini 3.5 Flash API
learn.oneLineDescription: GA frontier Flash model: beats Gemini 3.1 Pro on agent benchmarks at $1.50/$9 per 1M tokens.

detail.whatItDoes:
Gemini 3.5 Flash is Google's first Gemini 3.5-series model, launched generally available May 19, 2026. It beats Gemini 3.1 Pro on coding and agentic benchmarks — 76.2% Terminal-Bench 2.1 vs 70.3% for 3.1 Pro, 83.6% MCP Atlas — while running 4x faster and costing ~40% less ($1.50/$9 per 1M vs $2/$12 for 3.1 Pro). The model ID is `gemini-3.5-flash` (no preview suffix). It has a 1M-token context window, accepts text, image, audio, video, and PDF input, and ships with dynamic thinking on by default at medium level.

Key new API primitive shipping alongside the model: the Interactions API (beta), which provides server-side conversation history management — Google's equivalent of OpenAI's Responses API pattern. Managed Agents in the Gemini API is also live: a single call to the Antigravity agent provisions a remote Linux sandbox where the agent reasons, calls tools, and executes code.
detail.whoItsFor: API builders replacing Gemini 3.1 Pro in cost-sensitive agentic pipelines — the benchmark inversion means 3.5 Flash is the better default for coding and tool-use workloads. Also the right drop-in for teams migrating off `gemini-3-flash-preview`, and for anyone evaluating alternatives to Claude Opus 4.7 or GPT-5.5 at lower cost. Gemini 2.0 Flash users must migrate before June 1, 2026 when that model is deprecated.
pros: Beats Gemini 3.1 Pro on coding and agentic benchmarks at 40% lower cost — unusual Pro/Flash hierarchy inversion
1M-token context window with 90% cached-input discount ($0.15/M cached) cuts costs significantly for RAG-heavy apps
Parallel function calling and MCP Atlas-leading multi-tool coordination (83.6%)
Thinking levels (minimal/low/medium/high) let you tune cost vs. reasoning depth per-request
Available same-day on Gemini API, AI Studio, Vertex AI, Antigravity — no waitlist
cons: GPT-5.5 still leads on general reasoning benchmarks and Terminal-Bench 2.0 (82.7% vs 76.2%)
thinking_level default changed from `high` to `medium` vs. preview — silent regression for migrated prompts
3x price jump from Gemini 3 Flash Preview ($0.50/$3) — existing Flash Preview users will see a significant cost increase
Gemini 3.5 Pro (higher capability) not yet available; slated for June 2026
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Google account with API access at [aistudio.google.com](https://aistudio.google.com)
- `GEMINI_API_KEY` from AI Studio (free tier: 1,500 req/day on Flash models)
- Python 3.9+ or Node 20+ for the SDK examples below
- **Gemini 2.0 Flash users:** migrate before June 1, 2026 — that model is deprecated

## Get an API key

```bash
# Set in your environment
export GEMINI_API_KEY="your-key-here"
```

## Python quickstart

```bash
pip install google-genai
```

```python
import google.generativeai as genai
import os

genai.configure(api_key=os.environ["GEMINI_API_KEY"])

model = genai.GenerativeModel(
    model_name="gemini-3.5-flash",
    generation_config={
        "thinking_level": "high",  # explicit — default is 'medium', lower than old preview
    }
)

response = model.generate_content(
    "Write a Python function to parse ISO-8601 dates with timezone handling."
)
print(response.text)
```

## Node.js / TypeScript quickstart

```bash
npm install @google/generative-ai
```

```typescript
import { GoogleGenerativeAI } from "@google/generative-ai";

const genAI = new GoogleGenerativeAI(process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY!);

const model = genAI.getGenerativeModel({
  model: "gemini-3.5-flash",
  generationConfig: {
    thinkingLevel: "high", // set explicitly; default 'medium' is a regression from preview
  },
});

const result = await model.generateContent("Explain context caching in one paragraph.");
console.log(result.response.text());
```

## Managed Agent (one-call sandbox)

```python
# Spin up a full agent with a remote Linux sandbox — no infra setup
from google import genai

client = genai.Client(api_key=os.environ["GEMINI_API_KEY"])

# Interactions API (beta) — server-side history management
response = client.interactions.create(
    model="gemini-3.5-flash",
    agent="antigravity",  # provisions remote sandbox
    message="Clone the repo, run the test suite, and report failures."
)
print(response.output)
```

## Cost estimation

| Workload | Tokens/request | Cost at $1.50/$9 |
|----------|---------------|------------------|
| Chat (1K in / 500 out) | 1.5K | ~$0.0057 |
| RAG (10K in cached / 1K out) | 11K | ~$0.011 (cached input saves 90%) |
| Long agent run (100K in / 10K out) | 110K | ~$0.24 |

## Gotchas
- **`thinking_level` migration:** if your code sets `thinking_budget` (integer), that param is deprecated. Switch to `thinking_level` string enum: `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`. The default dropped from `high` to `medium` — explicitly set `high` for complex reasoning tasks or you will silently get less reasoning.
- **Model ID change:** use `gemini-3.5-flash` (no preview suffix). The old `gemini-3-flash-preview` id still works temporarily but is deprecated.
- **Gemini 2.0 Flash deprecation:** June 1, 2026. If you have any `gemini-2.0-flash` calls in production, update them now.

learn.name: ml-intern (Hugging Face)
learn.oneLineDescription: Open-source autonomous ML agent that researches, fine-tunes, and ships models via Hugging Face.

detail.whatItDoes:
ml-intern is an agentic loop (up to 300 iterations) that autonomously handles end-to-end ML tasks: reading papers, finding relevant Hugging Face datasets, fine-tuning models in a sandbox, uploading training traces to a private HF dataset, and delivering results without requiring step-by-step supervision. It supports two modes: interactive chat for exploratory work, and single-prompt headless execution for fully automated runs (e.g., 'fine-tune this model on this dataset and push the weights'). Every agent run produces a debuggable artifact stored as a private HF dataset, not a vanished terminal session.

The project reached 8,100 stars in its first few weeks on GitHub, driven by the practical overlap between ML engineers who need fine-tuning runs and agent workflows that can manage the iteration loop. It has built-in approval gates for sensitive operations (model pushes, external API calls) so it does not run fully blind.
detail.whoItsFor: ML engineers and researchers who need to run frequent fine-tuning experiments and want to offload the boilerplate: dataset search, hyperparameter setup, job monitoring, and weight pushing. Particularly useful for small teams without dedicated MLOps staff. Requires a Hugging Face account with write permissions and API token.
pros: Full ML pipeline automation: paper reading, dataset selection, training, and HF push in one agent run
Every session produces a private HF dataset artifact — debuggable, shareable, not lost on terminal close
Built-in approval gates prevent accidental pushes or external API calls without confirmation
Headless single-prompt mode for CI/CD integration: trigger a fine-tune run from a script or cron job
cons: 300-iteration cap can hit limits on large training jobs — monitor for early truncation on long runs
Requires HF Pro or institutional access for private dataset storage of training traces at scale
Approval gate UX is interactive-first; headless mode requires explicit flag overrides for unattended pipelines
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Python 3.10+
- Hugging Face account with write API token (`HF_TOKEN`)
- An LLM API key for the agent backbone (supports OpenAI, Anthropic, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint)
- Optional: GPU instance or HF Spaces for actual model training

## Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/huggingface/ml-intern
cd ml-intern
pip install -e .
```

## Set environment variables

```bash
export HF_TOKEN="hf_your_token_here"
export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-your-key"  # or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for Claude backbone
```

## Interactive mode

```bash
ml-intern chat
# Then type:
# > Find a sentiment classification dataset in French, fine-tune distilbert-base-multilingual-cased, push weights to my org
```

## Headless / single-prompt mode

```bash
ml-intern run \
  --prompt "Fine-tune Llama-3.2-1B on the HF 'imdb' dataset for 3 epochs. Push weights to my-org/imdb-llama-finetune." \
  --max-iterations 150
```

## Review the run artifact

```python
from datasets import load_dataset

# ml-intern uploads traces to a private dataset named after the run ID
trace_ds = load_dataset("your-hf-username/ml-intern-traces", split="latest")
print(trace_ds[0]["steps"])  # Full step-by-step agent log
```

## Gotchas
- **Approval gates are interactive by default.** To run fully headless, pass `--auto-approve pushes` — but review what it is about to push first by running with `--dry-run` once.
- **Max iterations:** the default cap is 300. Large fine-tuning jobs on big datasets may time out. Pass `--max-iterations 300` explicitly and monitor the trace dataset mid-run.
- **LLM backbone cost:** the agent issues many tool calls per iteration. Use a Flash-tier or cost-efficient model as the backbone (e.g., `gemini-3.5-flash`) to avoid large backbone bills on long runs.
